title: Blinding and randomization
objective: Explain how blinding and randomization prevent bias from shaping a result.

steps.title: Expectation leaks into measurement
steps.body: When you know which animal is the 'treated' one, that knowledge quietly shapes judgment calls — where to draw an ROI, how to score a behavior, which blots to re-run. **[[blinding]]** means the person measuring or scoring doesn't know the group identity, so expectation can't tilt the result. It matters most for any subjective or hand-scored readout.

steps.title: Randomize to break confounds
steps.body: Randomly assign animals to groups and randomize the order you process them. Otherwise a confound rides along: if all controls are run on Monday and all treated on Friday, 'treatment' is tangled with day, batch, and reagent age. Randomization spreads those nuisances evenly across groups.

steps.prompt: Which readout benefits MOST from blinding?
steps.explanation: Hand-scoring is subjective, so the scorer's expectation can bias it — exactly where blinding pays off. Fully automated, objective readouts are less vulnerable (though blinding still helps downstream analysis choices).

variants.setup: You're deciding where blinding matters most in a study.
variants.prompt: Which readout benefits most from a blinded scorer?
variants.reveal: Subjective, human-scored measures are the most bias-prone; automated numeric readouts are far less so.

steps.setup: You process all vehicle mice in week 1 and all [[actuator]] mice in week 2, unblinded.
steps.prompt: Why is the result hard to interpret even if it's 'significant'?
options: There's no problem; the two weeks act as independent replicates
Treatment is confounded with week/batch, and unblinded scoring adds bias
You simply used too many mice, which inflates the significance
The actuator cannot possibly work across two different weeks
steps.reveal: Any week-to-week difference (reagents, health, your technique) is now baked into the 'treatment' effect, and unblinded scoring can nudge it further. Interleave groups within each session and blind the scorer.

variants.prompt: Treated mice ran in week 1, controls in week 2, and scoring wasn't blinded. Why is even a 'significant' result hard to interpret?
options: There's no problem; the two weeks act as independent replicates
Treatment is confounded with week/batch, and unblinded scoring adds bias
You simply used too many mice, which inflates the significance
The actuator cannot possibly work across two different weeks
variants.explanation: You can't separate the treatment from the week/batch, and unblinded scoring can skew it — confounds, not biology.

reviewNotes: Blinding + randomization are cheap and high-impact; emphasize for behavior readouts.
